findings.title: Call to nonexistent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition in the repository is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160), and a grep finds no other overload. The `services` module therefore fails to compile, and everything depending on it fails with it. Pass the user, e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. Also check what the condition means: with the current helper (see the next finding) `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true exactly when the user is set and passkeys are off. That gives the intended behaviour: skip the form only when passkeys are disabled.

findings.title: `user != null` in isConditionalPasskeysEnabled disables passkeys on the normal (anonymous) login page
findings.body:
The helper returns true only when `user != null`. It now gates both `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in `authenticate` (line 115) and in `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137). The old code called `fillContextForm` in the anonymous case (`context.getUser() == null` at the old line 137, and the old block in the `else` branch of `authenticate`). With the new condition an anonymous user (no user set yet) never gets `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, the challenge or the rpId. The login page then has no `//form[@id='webauth']` and no conditional-UI autocomplete. The same applies to the error page after a bad username.

This contradicts the comment at line 114 ("setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled") and the PR's goal of enabling passkeys during re-authentication in addition to normal login. It also breaks the existing tests in this PR: `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey` open a fresh login and expect the passkey form (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:196). The helper should not depend on the user: `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. If the `user` parameter stays, drop the `!= null` check. If it goes, `UsernameForm` and the two call sites need updating.

findings.title: Missing @Override on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators
findings.body: This method overrides the protected hook added in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` (line 128) but has no `@Override`. If the signature drifts, the compiler will not flag it and the override silently stops working. Add `@Override`.

findings.title: try/catch(Exception) around fail() makes the 'no webauthn form' assertion unclear
findings.body: `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException`, which the `catch (Exception)` swallows, so the `assertThat(..., nullValue())` is never evaluated. Any other exception (a driver or timeout error) would also be swallowed and the test would pass. The sibling tests in this PR use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` for this check. Use that here as well (lines 291-297 and 312-318).

contracts.action: Re-authentication (user already set) now fills passkey conditional-UI data on the username/password form and on the username form
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code filled the passkey form data only when no user was set (old authenticate branch and challenge())
contracts.before_after: Before: passkeys only for anonymous users. After: the condition `user != null` in isConditionalPasskeysEnabled (line 161) means passkeys are filled only when a user is set, and not for anonymous users. This inverts the previous behaviour instead of extending it.
contracts.visible_effect: Normal login page loses the passkey form and conditional-UI autocomplete; the re-authentication page gets them.
contracts.failure_mode: Anonymous logins lose passkeys silently, with no error. UsernameForm does not compile (no-arg call).

contracts.action: Passkey (webauthn) submission during re-authentication, and the error challenge after a failed passkey
contracts.equivalent_path: AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler (line 222), now using the same shared AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError helper
contracts.before_after: The passkey failure path now hides the username and registration the same way as the password failure path, based on the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note. WebAuthnAuthenticator.action still rejects a passkey whose userHandle differs from context.getUser() (WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER), so re-authentication cannot switch users.
contracts.visible_effect: The error page after a failed passkey during re-authentication keeps the 're-authenticate' form layout.
contracts.failure_mode: The helper reads the auth note directly, so a stale note from an earlier anonymous pass is cleared by authenticate() (line 104). I found no defect here.

summary: The change as written does not work. UsernameForm.java:47 calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but only the one-argument version exists, so `services` will not compile. The helper at UsernamePasswordForm.java:161 also requires `user != null`, which would remove passkeys from the normal anonymous login page and break the existing passkey login tests in this PR. Two smaller points: `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` lacks `@Override`, and two tests swallow all exceptions in a try/catch around `fail()`. I only read the code; nothing was built or run.
